C. Vapor pressures are not always below or at 1 bar. This is false because when a liquid boils, its vapor pressure equals the ambient pressure, which can be above 1 bar (for example, at higher pressures).

D. When the vapor pressure of a liquid reaches the ambient pressure, it begins to boil. This is true because boiling occurs when the vapor pressure equals the surrounding pressure.
